name: Evaluate observations in light of hypotheses
description: The process of assessing the probability or strength of the observations under each of two or more competing hypotheses, and expressing the strength of support for one over another.
details: In evaluative mode the hypotheses are fixed before evaluation begins and are taken as given, typically from DFT-1195; this technique does not formulate or revise them. The examiner assesses how probable or strong the observations are under each hypothesis in turn, assuming each to be true. Assigning a probability or strength to the observations under a hypothesis requires knowledge of how the system behaves under that hypothesis, drawn from DFT-1090 or from published data. The technique concludes with the strength of support expressed as a likelihood ratio, its verbal equivalent, or other method. Conveying that opinion is DFT-1093.
